verdicts.summary:
This closes the critic's main gap in the item overlay: when you aren't editing, each block's Markdown now reads as a formatted document in the Geist body face. Inline code shows as faint mono chips, a fenced block is a tinted mono code block, and lists, headings and bold text render properly, so no backticks or ``` fences show.

How it works: in web/src/kit/TextArea.tsx, any text area with a head strip (the item editor's content: AGENTS.md blocks, an agent's instructions, a SKILL.md) stacks a rendered layer over its textarea in one grid cell. The rendered layer is hidden from screen readers and lets clicks through. At rest the textarea's text is transparent, so you see the rendered layer. A click lands in the source at roughly that spot. While the textarea has focus the rendered layer hides and you edit the raw source in place. On blur it reads formatted again.

The renderer is about 20 lines and handles paragraphs, `-`/`*` lists, `#` headings, ``` fences, `code` and **strong**. The CSS is in Form.module.css (.read and .prose) and uses existing tokens only (--chip-hover, --fs-tk, --font-mono), so there are no new colours. `.sheet:has(> .leaf:focus)` became `.sheet:has(.leaf:focus)` so the lit hairline still works inside the new wrapper. I updated the TextArea `head` entry in ledger.json and the header comments in TextArea.tsx and features/library/content.tsx.

The same rendering also shows in the library's editors, because they use the same item editor. A separate click-through run (scratchpad\g2\ovtest) checked that clicking edits the source, Unsaved changes appears, and blur goes back to the formatted view. It also checked the library file and agent editors. Nothing else in the piece changed: the peek and workflow overlay shots look the same as before.
